claims.text: Selective laser melting can introduce controlled porosity into HfMoTaTiZr.
Introducing controlled porosity will reduce the bulk density of HfMoTaTiZr.
Porous selectively laser-melted HfMoTaTiZr will retain a complex microstructure.
The retained complex microstructure and high-entropy-alloy effects will prevent a significant loss of mechanical strength despite the porosity.
Selective laser melting with controlled porosity will decrease density relative to as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
Room-temperature mechanical strength will be maintained or only slightly reduced relative to as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
Elevated-temperature mechanical strength, including at approximately 1000 °C, will be maintained relative to as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
The proposed intervention is intended to apply from room temperature through 1000 °C.
The proposed loading boundary includes tensile and compressive loading.
The mechanical consequences of the intervention depend on the extent of porosity introduced.
Oxidation may affect performance at elevated temperatures.
The proposed experiment compares density, tensile strength, compressive strength, and hardness of as-cast and porous selectively laser-melted HfMoTaTiZr at room temperature and 1000 °C.
A mechanical-strength decrease greater than 10% at either room temperature or 1000 °C relative to the as-cast material will falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The main hypothesis says mechanical properties will not be compromised, whereas the predicted outcome permits slightly reduced room-temperature strength.
The categorical claim of no compromise conflicts with a falsification rule that accepts mechanical-strength losses of up to 10%.
